sentences.text: Fire protection is designed to detect smoke, heat, and flame early enough to support automatic equipment protection and a controlled personnel response.
The Fire Detection Panel supervises detection circuits and annunciates alarms with location and fault information.
Detection coverage includes electrical enclosures, machinery spaces, and other areas identified by the site fire risk assessment.
The Turbine Sensor Bus carries equipment status used by protective functions and operational monitoring.
The Turbine Controller initiates the configured shutdown response when a confirmed fire condition requires turbine protection.
The Pitch System moves the blades to the defined safe position when commanded during an emergency shutdown.
The Rotor Brake Unit applies braking only in accordance with the turbine protection sequence and operating limits.
The Converter Cabinet is isolated when fire or overheating threatens electrical equipment or personnel.
The Nacelle Condition Monitor provides condition information that can help distinguish a developing equipment fault from a confirmed fire alarm.
At the Offshore Substation, fire detection and equipment protection are coordinated with electrical isolation procedures.
The Main Transformer is protected by site-specific detection and trip settings that account for its design and operating conditions.
Alarm priorities distinguish immediate danger from supervisory faults that require assessment but do not indicate an active fire.
An alarm is not cleared solely because a detector signal has returned to normal.
The Shore Control Room assesses incoming alarms, confirms the affected asset, and initiates the response appropriate to the reported severity.
The Control Engineer verifies the equipment state and checks that protection actions have completed before authorizing any further operational action.
The SCADA Gateway supports alarm visibility at the shore operating position without replacing local emergency controls.
The Electrical Technician performs local inspection only after the area has been assessed as safe and the required electrical isolations are in place.
A Turbine Lockout prevents remote restart while personnel investigate a fire alarm or complete post-event checks.
The Emergency Generator supports essential functions when normal electrical supplies are unavailable, subject to its designated load priorities.
Offshore personnel follow posted escape routes and muster at the designated assembly point when evacuation is ordered.
The Personnel Tracking Console supports accountability checks for personnel assigned to the affected work area.
The Operations Radio Console provides a coordinated communications channel for response instructions and status reports.
The Vessel Master maintains a safe position and readiness to support personnel recovery when directed by the response lead.
The HSE Officer advises on exposure, evacuation, and re-entry criteria in coordination with the incident response team.
The Field Supervisor confirms work party status and reports unresolved personnel or access concerns to the Shore Control Room.
